Only one post-denial recovery probe is admitted across threads/loops by the access-state guard. Validated HTTP200 clears the local denial; malformed/unavailable/error/cancelled recovery remains bounded and does not fabricate birth or poison token-negative caches. Other resources and retained original positive birth context remain independent.

Observed in-memory credential generation separates new coalescence and negative-cache contexts from older requests. Obsolete observed-context responses cannot set health/cache; headers use the captured credential. No credential is read from or written to an account/file by this change, and no automatic .env hot reload is claimed.

Native birth enrichment reports denial/recovery/probe/clock states before additional creation reservations. Authorization failures are not cached as token-specific missing birth. Known original birth, queue residence, per-minute spacing and all existing entry/risk/size guards remain intact.

Builtin numeric seconds now is compared at its original precision, not rounded through datetime. Exact equal receipt can pass, strictly future receipt fails, and nested birth merge retains the original numeric limit. Datetime/string/millisecond compatibility remains; no future tolerance, history relabeling or operational-profit effect is claimed.

A plain slots negative marker preserves unregistered-spec cold import. The legacy sentinel name is retained for existing integrations, but new failures use context-bound markers and unbound markers invalidate. Only the new optional-default env key is added to strict existing parity exclusions; personal .env/mandatory Prime flags/duplicate checks are not relaxed or rewritten.
